claims.statement: Current Polish law requires stores above 200 square metres to contract with every system operator that approaches them, requires deposit settlement at intervals no longer than a month, and requires detailed retailer records of products, returns, and deposit amounts.
The Ministry's current operator page lists eight authorized deposit-system operators, establishing a genuinely multi-operator market structure.
The Ministry reported 3.2 billion returned containers, more than 60,000 return points, and 17,500 RVM-equipped points by 21 August 2026, with RVMs handling 88 percent of returns.

PolKa's own rules describe real-time POS/RVM integration, weekly manual reporting, access to invoices and accounting notes, and built-in verification of quantities and values used to settle collection points.

COMP markets a multi-operator retailer panel with settlement visibility, existing fiscal/POS integration, and monthly packages from 19.90 to 79.90 PLN net, directly covering much of the original product scope.
Insoft already integrates PC-Market and PC-POS with COMP DRS and Zwrotka and includes cashier and return-settlement reports.

contrary_evidence: COMP already sells multi-operator handling, reports, settlement visibility, and third-party integrations at 19.90-79.90 PLN net per store monthly.
PolKa's operator system already integrates transaction feeds, provides accounting documents, and verifies data forming the basis of retailer settlement.
Insoft embeds DRS collection and settlement reports directly in established retail software.
The system's rapid live scale indicates that core infrastructure and major channel relationships are already deployed.

economics.acquisition_route: Reconcile one closed month for one multi-store retailer, quantify recovered cash and avoided finance labour, then pursue accounting and POS partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The prior 250 PLN-per-store assumption is contradicted by low-priced incumbent operational software. At the observed competitive price band, a 5 million PLN founder-net-worth path is not evidenced and would require validated chain-level audit fees, high retention, efficient partner distribution, and likely expansion beyond a small Polish niche.
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-16 hours weekly for one bounded pilot, with connector and onboarding work delegated only after repeatability is demonstrated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software and analyst-assisted exception review less connector maintenance, secure data handling, and support; per-event processing revenue is not assumed
economics.payback: Payback exists only if recovered settlement leakage plus avoided close effort exceeds the audit fee; no public evidence quantifies the variance pool
economics.pricing: Unvalidated pilot hypothesis: 5,000-15,000 PLN for a chain-level historical audit, then 20-80 PLN per location monthly for exception monitoring; this must beat or complement COMP operational tiers advertised at 19.90-79.90 PLN net per store monthly
economics.retention_or_repeat: The law caps financial settlement periods at one month and retail records recur, but paid retention beyond incumbent reports is unvalidated

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned mapping of retailer formats, operator documents, exception causes, and resolution outcomes can reduce audit effort, subject to contractual data-reuse rights
fingerprint.customer: Polish grocery, franchise, and wholesale groups with multiple stores above 200 square metres and heterogeneous POS, RVM, or operator paths
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell a one-month audit through retail accounting advisers and integrate through willing POS, RVM, accounting, or DRS technology partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Read-only cross-system exception audit, variance classification, cash expectation, and operator-ready evidence packets sold as a chain setup plus low per-location subscription; no deposit custody, collection operation, or official settlement role
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A central retail finance or compliance team pays for an initial historical exception audit and then for monthly monitoring when an evidence-backed exception file is closed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: At monthly close, the retailer's legally required deposit records, operator documents, collection counts, and cash reimbursements do not agree and the existing operational host does not explain the exception

founder_fit: Event matching and anomaly triage fit the founder's data-science and automation skills
A historical read-only audit can be piloted part-time without handling regulated deposit funds
Central finance buyers and integration partners reduce dependence on high-energy consumer selling or a personal brand
risks: The exception pool may be too small after incumbent reconciliation
Operator and POS contracts may block data access or derived-data reuse
Incumbents can add exception workflows using existing integrations and distribution
Low per-store pricing can make custom connectors and support uneconomic
False discrepancy alerts can damage retailer-operator relationships
Sensitive transaction and bank data create security and procurement burdens

structure.commercial_archetype: Exception-audit SaaS for multi-store retail finance
structure.control_point: The normalized, evidence-linked exception between the retailer's own sales, returns, collections, operator documents, and cash receipt
structure.critical_dependency: Retailers must be able and willing to export sufficiently granular data from each relevant POS, RVM, operator portal, and accounting system

thesis: Polish retail groups operating stores above 200 square metres face monthly deposit settlement, store-level recordkeeping, and potentially several operator relationships. Current operator, COMP, and POS products already automate core collection and settlement cheaply, so the remaining testable wedge is a read-only finance-control layer that compares retailer-authorized POS, RVM, collection, operator-document, and bank data, classifies only unexplained exceptions, and creates evidence packets without holding deposits or performing statutory operator duties.
title: Deposit Exception Audit Poland
uncertainties: Frequency, causes, and monetary size of unexplained retailer-operator variances after incumbent tooling is used
Whether operator portals and retail systems expose lawful, sufficiently granular exports or APIs to an independent auditor
Whether retailer contracts permit third-party processing and reuse of resolution data
Whether central finance teams will pay separately for exception assurance rather than rely on their POS vendor, operator, or accountant
Whether the proposed chain-level setup and subscription prices produce demonstrable payback
How many target chains actually operate heterogeneous multi-operator paths rather than one integrated host
